# RSOS restriction and unitary subtheories {#sec-rsos}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false title="Learning goals"}
- Restrict a $U_q(\hat g)$-symmetric theory at a root of unity to an RSOS theory.
- Identify the restricted theories with perturbed minimal and $W$-algebra models.
- Understand Hermitian analyticity, and why IRF bases can restore unitarity.
:::

The imaginary-coupling theories are not unitary, but some of their restrictions are. At special couplings, where $q$ is a root of unity, the quantum-group symmetry allows a consistent truncation of the space of states, and the truncated theories are perturbed minimal models, some unitary and some not. This chapter explains the restriction, identifies the restricted theories, and asks when the result is unitary. @sec-sg-quantum-group did this for sine-Gordon; here the general case is treated, ending with an exact criterion for the fundamental kinks of $a_2^{(1)}$.

## Quantum-group restriction {#sec-qg-restriction}

At a root of unity the representation theory of $U_q(g)$ truncates (@sec-roots-of-unity): only finitely many irreducible representations have nonzero quantum dimension, and their tensor products, with the quantum-dimension-zero summands discarded, close on themselves. The S-matrix of the solitons commutes with $U_q(\hat g^\vee)$, so it can be written in the IRF form of @sec-irf. Its states are then labelled by sequences of heights, highest weights $a_0,a_1,\dots,a_N$ with $L(a_{k+1})\subset L(a_k)\otimes V$, and the heights are interpreted as vacua between kinks.

**Restriction** keeps only the heights in the finite set allowed at the root of unity. Because the face weights never connect allowed heights to disallowed ones, the restricted S-matrix still satisfies the Yang–Baxter equation, unitarity, crossing and the bootstrap. The restricted theory has finitely many vacua and kinks interpolating between them [@reshetikhin1990; @leclair1989; @smirnov1991].

For $a_n^{(1)}$ with $\beta^2/4\pi=p/p'$, $p<p'$ coprime, $q$ is a root of unity and the allowed heights are the weights of $su(n+1)$ at level $p-n-1$. For $n=1$ these are the spins $j\le(p-2)/2$ of @sec-roots-of-unity; for $n=2$ they are the level-$(p-3)$ weights used in @prp-rsos-kinks.

Two features of restriction matter for unitarity.

- **Breathers are singlets.** Restriction acts on the quantum-group labels, and breathers carry none. Their amplitudes with kinks and with each other are untouched by the restriction. A sector that is $\Theta$-broken because of breathers stays broken.
- **The basis changes.** The IRF basis is not the soliton basis. Eigenvalues of transfer matrices are basis-independent, but Hermitian analyticity is not, so restriction can change whether a QFT inner product exists.

## Perturbed minimal and $W$ models {#sec-perturbed-minimal}

The conformal Toda theory based on the finite algebra $g$ at imaginary coupling is a free-field realization of a $W$-algebra conformal field theory, and the affine Toda theory perturbs it by the vertex operator of the affine root $\vec\alpha_0$. After restriction, the conformal theory becomes a minimal model of the $W$-algebra, and the perturbation becomes one of its primary fields. The known cases are:

| affine Toda theory | restricted theory |
|---|---|
| $a_1^{(1)}$ (sine-Gordon), $\beta^2/4\pi=p/p'$ | $\mathcal M(p,p')+\phi_{1,3}$ (@prp-sg-rsos) |
| $a_2^{(2)}$ | $\mathcal M(p,p')+\phi_{1,2}$ or $\phi_{2,1}$ [@smirnov1991; @efthimiou1993] |
| $a_n^{(1)}$, $\beta^2/4\pi=p/p'$ | $W_{n+1}(p,p')$ minimal model perturbed by the field of the adjoint representation; for $n=2$ see @prp-rsos-kinks |
| other algebras | perturbations of $W$-algebra minimal models, studied in [@takacs1997a; @takacs1997b; @takacs1997c; @tkw1997] |

Examples include the thermal perturbation of the 3-state Potts model, $W_3(4,5)$, the $\phi_{1,2}$ perturbation of $\mathcal M(3,4)$, which is the Ising model in a magnetic field, and the scaling Lee–Yang model, which arises from both sine-Gordon and $a_2^{(2)}$ (@sec-lee-yang).

The unitary minimal models are those with $p'=p+1$, and in the cases checked their perturbations have unitary S-matrices. The others are non-unitary, and some of them have complex finite-volume spectra, observed directly in the truncated conformal space approach [@tkw1997; @tw2002].

## Hermitian analyticity and IRF bases {#sec-hermitian-analyticity-irf}

By @sec-unitarity-crossing-intro, a braiding-unitary S-matrix is unitary in the QFT sense exactly when it is also Hermitian analytic, $S(\theta)^\dagger=S(-\theta^*)$, in some basis of one-particle states [@miramontes1999]. For quantum-group S-matrices in the soliton (vertex) basis this generally fails, because the $*$-structure of $U_q$ at $\lvert q\rvert=1$ reverses tensor factors (@sec-qg-hermitian). In the IRF basis the situation can be different. The face weights are built from $q$-Clebsch–Gordan coefficients, whose normalization involves square roots of quantum dimensions. If all quantum dimensions of the allowed heights are positive, these can be chosen real, and the face weights become Hermitian analytic. Hoare, Hollowood and Miramontes [-@hoare2013] showed this for the $U_q(su(2)^{(1)})$-based S-matrices of $q$-deformed world-sheet theories and generalized sine-Gordon models. When some quantum dimensions are negative, square roots of negative numbers enter, and Hermitian analyticity can fail in a way no rescaling of states can repair. @prp-rsos-kinks makes this precise for $a_2^{(1)}$.

## Unitary subtheories {#sec-unitary-subtheories}

At $q$ a root of unity, RSOS restriction replaces the Krein space by the space of states of a perturbed minimal model, which carries a positive inner product when the minimal model is unitary. The transfer-matrix eigenvalues after restriction are a *different* set from those before [@tw1999]. So restriction can cure a broken sector, but it cannot touch quantum-group singlets such as breathers.

::: {#cnj-unitary-rsos}
**[Conjecture]** An RSOS-restricted ATFT has a unitary S-matrix if and only if its restricted S-matrix, including the breather amplitudes, is Hermitian analytic in some basis of one-particle states [@miramontes1999]. We conjecture that this holds exactly when (i) the underlying minimal CFT is unitary and (ii) every sector surviving the restriction is $\Theta$-unbroken. Unitarity of the field theory requires in addition positive bound-state residues (U5). The scaling Lee–Yang model, whose S-matrix is a pure phase but whose residue has the wrong sign, shows that Hermitian analyticity alone does not suffice for that.

:::

Evidence:

- the de Vega–Fateev unitary $W_3$ series, at couplings where breathers decouple;
- $M_{6,7}+\Phi_{1,2}$, unitary;
- $M_{3,14}+\Phi_{1,5}$, where TCSA confirms a complex spectrum [@tkw1997; @tw1999];
- the $U_q(su(2)^{(1)})$-based S-matrices of Hoare, Hollowood and Miramontes [-@hoare2013], whose IRF form at $q$ a root of unity is manifestly Hermitian analytic and hence unitary. This is the mechanism by which restriction restores unitarity.
- the RSOS-restricted fundamental kinks of $a_2^{(1)}$ (@prp-rsos-kinks), the first higher-rank case. For $p'=p+1$ (i) and (ii) hold and the S-matrix is unitary. For $p'\equiv\pm1\pmod p$ with $p'\ne p+1$ the kink S-matrix is unitary although (i) fails; these models all contain breathers, whose amplitudes with kinks are not phases [@tw1999, eq. 3.7], so (ii) fails as well and the full S-matrix is not unitary. For the other couplings tested the kink S-matrix is already not unitary.

::: {#prp-rsos-kinks}
## RSOS kinks of $a_2^{(1)}$
**[Theorem, given a unitary and real-analytic scalar factor]** Let $\beta^2/4\pi=p/p'$ with $p<p'$ coprime and $p\ge4$. RSOS restriction gives the perturbed $W_3(p,p')$ minimal model, whose vacua are the level-$(p-3)$ weights of $su(3)$; for $W_3(4,5)$ this is the thermal 3-state Potts model. In the symmetric gauge the IRF S-matrix of the fundamental kinks is the Jimbo–Miwa–Okado face weight, whose off-diagonal factor $\sqrt{[A+1][A-1]}/[A]$ we write as $\sqrt{d_b}\sqrt{d_d}/(\sqrt{d_a}\sqrt{d_c})$, with per-height roots, which fixes its branch; $d_h$ is the quantum dimension of the height $h$. The kink–antikink part follows by crossing, and its scalar factor inherits real analyticity. We use $q=e^{i\pi(p'-p)/p}$ and crossing $u\to-\tfrac32-u$, with $u=3i\theta/2\pi$. This reproduces the moduli of the physical soliton–antisoliton amplitude in the conventions of [@tw1999, eqs. 3.1, 3.4], where $q=-e^{i\pi\lambda}$. Then:

1. If $p'\equiv\pm1\pmod p$, every $d_h$ is positive, the S-matrix is Hermitian analytic in all four sectors ($33$, $\bar3\bar3$, $3\bar3$, $\bar33$), and $SS^\dagger=1$ for real $\theta$. Every multi-kink transfer matrix is unitary.
2. If $p'\not\equiv\pm1\pmod p$, some soliton–soliton block has $d_ad_bd_cd_d<0$. No rescaling of kink states that preserves the vacuum labels, even a rapidity-dependent one, makes the S-matrix Hermitian analytic or unitary.

:::

::: {.proof}
1. Write $r=p'-p$ and $[x]=\sin(\pi rx/p)/\sin(\pi r/p)$. Then $\operatorname{sgn}[x+2]=\operatorname{sgn}[x]$ for all $1\le x\le p-3$ if and only if $r\equiv\pm1\pmod p$. Indeed, for $r=s+kp$ with $1\le s\le p-1$, $\operatorname{sgn}[x]=\pm(-1)^{\lfloor sx/p\rfloor+kx}$, and the increments of $\lfloor sx/p\rfloor$ lie in $\{0,1\}$, so the condition forces them to be constant on $[1,p-2]$, which gives $s\in\{1,p-1\}$.
2. If $r\equiv\pm1$, every $d_h>0$, so the gauge factors are real. Every weight is a real constant times $[x\pm u]$ or $[x\pm u\pm\tfrac32]$ with $u=3i\theta/2\pi$ imaginary for real $\theta$, so $\overline{w(\theta)}=w(-\theta)$. The gauge is symmetric under exchanging the in and out middle heights. This is Hermitian analyticity, and with braiding unitarity it gives $SS^\dagger=1$ [@miramontes1999]. Products of unitary kink S-matrices are unitary.
3. If $r\not\equiv\pm1$, step 1 gives some $A$ with $[A+1][A-1]<0$, and $A$ occurs as a height difference in a $2\times2$ soliton–soliton block. There $d_ad_bd_cd_d<0$, so the off-diagonal constant is imaginary and $\overline{S_{db}(\theta)}=-S'_{bd}(-\theta)$ for the reversed process $S'$. Unitarity in a positive diagonal metric would require $\overline{S_{db}}=(n^{\rm in}_b/n^{\rm out}_d)\,S'_{bd}(-\theta)$, so $n^{\rm in}_b/n^{\rm out}_d=-1$, which is impossible.

:::

*Numerics.* The mixed Yang–Baxter equations hold to $5\times10^{-15}$ and braiding unitarity to $8\times10^{-14}$ in all four sectors. Hermitian analyticity and $SS^\dagger=1$ hold to $10^{-12}$ at the eight couplings tested with $p'\equiv\pm1$, and fail by $O(1)$ at the five others. The sign criterion was checked by brute force for $4\le p\le60$. Scripts: `foundations_code/irf/`.

Three consequences follow.

- **Restriction cures the vertex-form breaking.** For $p'\equiv\pm1$ the three-soliton breaking of @prp-krein-fundamental and the soliton–antisoliton breaking of Takács and Watts both disappear: all restricted transfer matrices are unitary (part 1), and numerically unimodular to $3\times10^{-14}$ for up to six kinks. Breathers are present exactly when $3(p'-p)>2p$ [@tw1999, eq. 3.3]. Together with $p'\equiv\pm1$, their absence leaves only $p'=p+1$, the unitary $W_3$ series. For $p'\equiv\pm1$ with $p'\ne p+1$ the kink S-matrix is unitary, but these models contain breathers, and the kink–breather amplitude [@tw1999, eq. 3.7] is not a phase.
- **Unbroken does not imply Hermitian analytic.** For $p'=p+2$, for example $W_3(7,9)$, $W_3(9,11)$ and $W_3(11,13)$, every kink transfer matrix computed has unimodular eigenvalues, up to six kinks [Numerical]. These sectors are $\Theta$-unbroken but, by part 2, admit no Hermitian-analytic basis. The obstruction is the sign pattern of the quantum dimensions. Negative quantum dimensions occur only in non-unitary models, but not every non-unitary model has them: for $p'\equiv-1\pmod p$ all $d_h$ are positive. The unbrokenness of the $p'=p+2$ sectors depends on the sign of $q$, which the criterion of part 1 does not.
- **Krein pairs survive restriction.** For $p'-p\ge3$ with $p'\not\equiv\pm1$, for example $W_3(10,13)$, the restricted soliton–antisoliton transfer matrices already have eigenvalues off the unit circle at two kinks. They come in exact pairs $(s,1/\bar s)$ to $10^{-12}$, as Krein-unitarity requires; the Krein form itself is open (open problem 7).

This reduces H12 to a criterion that can be checked from the S-matrix.

## Exercises {#sec-rsos-exercises}

::: {#exr-allowed-heights}
For $U_q(sl_2)$ with $q=e^{i\pi/p}$, show that the spin-$\frac12$ IRF model restricted to heights $0\le j\le(p-2)/2$ is consistent: the face weights between allowed heights never require a disallowed one.
:::

::: {#exr-quantum-dims}
For $q=e^{i\pi r/p}$ with $r$ coprime to $p$, compute the quantum dimensions $[k]_q$, $1\le k\le p-1$, of the allowed spins. Show that all are positive if and only if $r\equiv\pm1\pmod{2p}$, that they alternate in sign if and only if $r\equiv p\pm1\pmod{2p}$, and that the ratios $[k+1]_q[k-1]_q/[k]_q^2$ are positive for all $2\le k\le p-2$ if and only if $r\equiv\pm1\pmod p$. Compare with step 1 of the proof of @prp-rsos-kinks.
:::

::: {#exr-lee-yang-restriction}
Show that sine-Gordon at $\beta^2/4\pi=2/5$ restricts to a theory with no kinks and one breather, and identify it as the scaling Lee–Yang model. Which unitarity property fails, and why can restriction not repair it?
:::

## Notes and references {#sec-rsos-notes}

Quantum-group restriction of sine-Gordon is due to LeClair [-@leclair1989], Smirnov [-@smirnov1991] and Reshetikhin and Smirnov [-@reshetikhin1990]; Efthimiou [-@efthimiou1993] treated $a_2^{(2)}$. Takács and collaborators studied the restrictions of higher affine Toda theories and their finite-volume spectra [@takacs1997a; @takacs1997b; @takacs1997c; @tkw1997], and Takács and Watts found the complex spectra [@tw1999; @tw2002]. Miramontes [-@miramontes1999] identified Hermitian analyticity as the missing condition, and Hoare, Hollowood and Miramontes [-@hoare2013] showed how IRF bases restore it. The criterion of @prp-rsos-kinks and @cnj-unitary-rsos are new here.
